problem.symptom: With the sample-path and codec-config-duplicate fixes, 4K120 records a well-formed mp4 (full video sample table, ffprobe reads HEVC 3840x2160) but ffmpeg cannot split the bitstream ('No start code is found. Error splitting the input into NAL units'); the video is still not decodable.
problem.cause: The vendor encoder emits the codec-specific data (VPS/SPS/PPS) length-prefixed as well, not Annex-B. makeHEVCCodecSpecificData sees that the buffer does not start with a 0x00000001 start code and falls back to copyHEVCCodecSpecificData, which copies the length-prefixed parameter sets verbatim as the hvcC. The stsd then carries a malformed hvcC (configurationVersion byte 0x00, i.e. a 4-byte length high byte, followed by a 23-byte length-prefixed VPS), so the decoder config does not match the length-prefixed samples.

evidence.ffmpeg_error: No start code is found. Error splitting the input into NAL units

fix.mechanism: Before make{AVC,HEVC}CodecSpecificData, run the same length-prefixed-to-Annex-B conversion (ConvertLengthPrefixedNalToAnnexB, added by the length-prefixed-NAL patch) on the codec-config buffer in place. The parameter sets then start with 0x00000001, so parseHEVCCodecSpecificData/parseAVCCodecSpecificData build a valid hvcC/avcC whose NAL length size matches the length-prefixed samples.
fix.scope: Only the codec-config buffer is converted; the buffer is released immediately after, and Annex-B input is left unchanged by the converter.

remaining: On-device confirmation that 4K120 and long 4K60 record a decodable HEVC track
